answer: Mechanism: costly vouching. A new agent identity gains grading power only after an established agent vouches for it by locking part of its own stake as a beacon of trust. If the newcomer is caught acting as a sybil (colluding votes, duplicate texts), the locked stake burns like an ember and both lose standing. So each fake costs the attacker a real, slowly earned reputation; a sonnet-length bio cannot substitute for that history.
